item.title: Tech Transfer Thursdays
item.description:
Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 5:30 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://mailchi.mp/rice/aug-20th-ion-event-landing-page Universities and research institutions produce some of the most valuable discoveries in the world, yet navigating the path to commercialize them is not always clear or well known. Houston’s universities and research institutions are partnering to to simplify the commercialization process. Mark your calendars for Thursday, August 20th for the launch of Tech Transfer Thursdays at The Ion District! I’m thrilled that the Rice University Office of Technology Transfer is teaming up with the tech transfer offices at Baylor College of Medicine and Houston Methodist for our first event in this monthly series. Together, we are partnering to spotlight the breakthrough innovations and technologies developed across our respective institutions, and show you exactly how to leverage this intellectual property (IP) to launch new ventures or create strategic growth opportunities for your business. Each month will feature a different domain focus, and we are kicking off August with Digital Health! Who Should Attend? 💡 Founders & Operators: Looking for breakthrough technology to serve as the foundation for your next venture or strengthen your IP moat. 🏢 Corporate Innovators: Seeking external research to bridge technical gaps, accelerate roadmaps, or unlock new business models. 📈 Investors & VCs: Searching for vetted, high-barrier-to-entry university spinouts and deep-tech startups. Event Snapshot: 5:30 PM: Open Networking & TTO Booths 6:00 PM: TTO Panel on the licensing & commercialization roadmap 6:40 PM: University Startup Pitch Spotlight 7:00 PM: Free Networking

item.title: Mapping Houston's Innovation Ecosystem
item.description:
Friday, August 21, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 027, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002

Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it. Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration. The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights. This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth. Ion’s Vision Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey. From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem. Who Should Attend? This session is ideal for: Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources. Investors curious about the local startup landscape. Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community. Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship. Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene. Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem. Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

From Ion District

item.title: Industrial Growth Series: Why Great Industrial Companies Stop Growing
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1996106693855?aff=oddtdtcreator Great industrial companies do not usually stop growing because they lack capability. They stop growing because the market changes around them. For years, many industrial companies have grown through strong relationships, repeat customers, referrals, reputation, and word of mouth. That approach can work for a long time. Until it does not. The company is still strong. The team still delivers. Customers still trust the work. The reputation is still solid. But new opportunities become harder to create. The same relationships are no longer producing the same volume of business. Referrals become less predictable. Buyers become harder to reach. Competitors become more visible. The company starts depending too heavily on the momentum it built in the past. That is where many great industrial companies get stuck. They are not failing. They have simply reached a point where the way they grew before may not be enough to support where they want to go next. This session of the Industrial Growth Series is designed to help owners, executives, and commercial leaders understand why strong industrial companies hit growth ceilings and what must begin to change to create new momentum. We will explore the role of market positioning, visibility, relationships, business development, diversification, and changing buyer behavior without turning the conversation into another tactical sales seminar. This is not about chasing every opportunity. It is not about abandoning the relationships that helped build the company. It is about recognizing when the market has changed and ensuring the company’s approach to growth changes with it. What You’ll Learn Why successful industrial companies eventually hit growth ceilings Why reputation, referrals, and repeat customers may stop producing the same results How changing markets and buyer behavior affect industrial growth Where commercial momentum commonly begins to slow Why strong capabilities do not always create strong market visibility How leaders can begin creating new paths to growth What established companies should evaluate before investing in more activity Who Should Attend Industrial company owners and CEOs Manufacturing leaders Energy, oil and gas, and field service companies Construction and infrastructure firms Commercial, sales, and business development leaders Companies with strong capabilities but inconsistent new opportunity flow Leaders working to break through a growth plateau Event Format 11:45 AM – 12:00 PM | Networking at the stairs 12:00 PM – 12:40 PM | Presentation 12:40 PM – 1:00 PM | Discussion and Q&A 1:00 PM – 1:15 PM | Networking at the stairs About the Speaker Jada Powell is the Founder of Powell Consulting Group, where she works with industrial, energy, oil and gas, construction, and service-based companies to build stronger commercial infrastructure and more consistent business development momentum. Her work focuses on helping mid-market companies move beyond relationship-only growth into more intentional, visible, and scalable commercial strategies. This session is part of the Industrial Growth Series, a three-part in-person series at The Ion focused on how established industrial companies can remain visible, competitive, and positioned for the next stage of growth.

From Ion District

item.title: Heights Garden Club Presents: Angel Wing Arts brings this Bee Watering Station Craft to the Heights Garden Club
item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Houston Heights City Hall & Fire Station, 107 W. 12th Street, Houston, TX, 77008, United States

AUGUST 26th at 6:30pm, join us at the Heights Fire Station Carolyn, of Angel Wing Arts, (Instagram @cacoatesart or @anglewingarts) and one of our own, will lead this workshop. Carolyn has been active in the arts for over 30 years, from faux finishes to murals to art pieces. She has worked with clients and their art needs, and her work itself is whimsical and fun. Please join us on August 26, at our favorite spot to mingle, the historic Heights Fire station on 12th and Yale streets. There will be a demo, and plenty of inspiration to kick off your creativity!! Each participant will construct two bee watering stations from clay pots and saucers and then decorate them with paints and pens, as seen in the photo. Let’s help our bees and butterflies in this heat by providing them a safe place to get a drink that YOU are providing with your cute, personalized vessel. Reserve your spot through Sign-Up Genius so we have an accurate headcount and can make sure we have the right amount of supplies on hand. But hurry, there is only room for 25 guests and the deadline to sign up is August 19th. $20 cash per person, ages 12 and up, to be paid at the door. Please, no unaccompanied minors. Doors opens at 6:30pm, Class is 7-9pm. Please arrive early so that instruction can begin on time. Water and some light refreshments will be provided, but please consider bringing a snack to share, if you are so inclined. You may bring your own adult beverages if you wish.

item.title: NASA Tech Talks: Rice University’s Space Humanities Initiative
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

We want HOU! Join us to discover NASA’s toughest tech challenges—and apply your skills and expertise to solve them. This month, NASA Tech Talks will feature Rice’s new Space Humanities Initiative, co-led by Alexander Regier, the William Faulkner Professor of English and chair of the Department of English and Creative Writing, and David Alexander, director of the Rice Space Institute and professor of physics and astronomy. Long before rockets, satellites or space stations, humans were already in a relationship with outer space. People looked up and named constellations. They told stories about the moon. They wrote poems, mapped stars and built myths around lights in the sky they could not touch. Across cultures and centuries, outer space functioned as more than a scientific mystery; it was a mirror for human longing, fear, imagination and hope. The Rice Space Initiative brings scholars across disciplines together to examine how culture, language, ethics and imagination shape space exploration, and how space exploration shapes them in return.  Please join us for a discussion of how the Initiative came to be, and how it might provide a sustained space where questions about ownership, settlement, commercial use and planetary responsibility can be addressed in an interdisciplinary manner. Please join us after the talk for drinks and networking at Second Draught!   About the Speakers Dr. David Alexander is an astrophysics professor at Rice University and a faculty scholar at the Baker Institute for Public Policy. He also serves as the Director of the Rice Space Institute. Alexander was awarded an OBE by her majesty Queen Elizabeth in 2018 for services to the space industry and was named a Chevalier of the National Order of Merit by the French Republic in 2026.  He received a Presidential Early Career Award in 2004 and was appointed a Kavli Frontiers Fellow by the National Academy of Sciences in 2006. Alexander has served on many professional committees including the NASA Advisory Council’s Heliophysics Subcommittee, and the NASA Solar Heliospheric Management and Operations Working Group.  He was named a GlobalScot by the Scottish government and served as an elected member of the Board of Directors of the American Astronautical Society from 2018-2022. He served as Chair of the Aerospace Industry Committee of the Greater Houston Partnership, been on the Board of the Houston Spaceport Development Corporation since 2021 and was recently appointed to the Texas Aerospace Research and Space Economy Consortium Executive Committee.  Alexander received his Bachelor’s degree and doctorate from the University of Glasgow. Alexander Regier is the William Faulkner Professor of English in the Department of English and Creative Writing. He also holds a full appointment in the Department of Modern and Classical Languages, Literatures and Cultures. Regier is the author and editor of multiple books and articles on literature, art, and culture. His publications cover a range of subjects, from eighteenth-century philosophy and Romantic literature to outer space, awkwardness, fragmentation, ruins, and sports. In recent years, Regier has received an Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship for Experienced Researchers, as well as Fellowships at the National Humanities Center, the Center for Research in the Arts, Social Sciences, and Humanities at the University of Cambridge, and a Visiting Fellowship at the University of Exeter. He has also won multiple awards, amongst others, from the National Endowment for the Humanities. From 2023 to 2026, he was chair of the Department of English and Creative Writing at Rice and is now co-director of the Space Humanities Initiative. Dario Robleto is an artist, writer, and filmmaker based in Houston, Texas. His work has been exhibited widely and is held in prominent collections, including the Harvard Art Museum, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C. He has held research fellowships and residencies at institutions including the Smithsonian Museum of American History, the SETI Institute, and the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University. From 2018 to 2023, he served as Artist-at-Large at Northwestern University’s McCormick School of Engineering and the Block Museum of Art. In 2020, he served as a research consultant for the popular science television series Cosmos: Possible Worlds. In 2016, Robleto was appointed Texas State 3-D Visual Artist, and in 2025, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters from Middlebury College. He is currently working on his first book, The Heartbeat at the Edge of the Solar System: Science, Emotion, and the Golden Record, co-authored with Harvard art historian Jennifer Roberts. It will be published by Scribner in 2027. Ryn Delpapa is a change-maker who believes in impact. A neuroarts tech founder, interdisciplinary artist, and speaker on a mission, they honor life’s biodiversity, from plants to people. Ryn is a recent 2026 TEDxHouston Countdown speaker, 2025 4.0 Tiny Fellow, and CXC Changemakers for the Planet Fellow, bridging creativity, health, and environmental stewardship within their venture, AR+E COMETS, a global health studio. As a 2024 City of Houston City Initiative grant awardee, their Art for Climate Resilience community arts-in-health program shaped community health in Houston’s Third and Fifth Wards. With a B.S. in International Nutrition from the University of Texas at Austin and a kaleidoscope career from Houston to Chengdu, China, their global health background, 8 years in B2B SaaS tech, and arts-in-health research enable them to bridge creativity and planetary health. Work they share through their venture, consultancy, and Earthly Bonds podcast, where they explore health, from brain to biosphere, for creative, resilient living. Montgomery B. Goforth has more than 40 years of experience as both Engineer and Manager in a variety of highly technical space and defense-related efforts.  After working for a small defense contractor specializing in anti-submarine warfare, he joined NASA’s Johnson Space Center in 1990.  He has held leadership positions in multiple JSC Directorates and Program Offices. In his previous role as Assistant Director of the JSC Engineering Directorate, he established a framework to better focus Engineering’s efforts towards Human Spaceflight technology and systems development consistent with JSC and Agency goals for exploration. Mr. Goforth is now serving as Acting Director of the Business Development & Technology Integration Office at JSC, and as the JSC Chief Technologist.  In these capacities he will be helping to expand the Houston Aerospace Community through the identification of opportunities to develop space/terrestrial technologies of interest to JSC and Human Space Exploration.  Mr. Goforth was born in East Texas, raised in Southern California and Arizona, and graduated from Rice University (BSME 1982, MSME 1987). About NASA Tech Talks In these presentations, occurring the fourth Thursdays of the month, Mr. Montgomery Goforth and other aerospace subject matter experts will discuss the technology development challenges faced by NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the surrounding Aerospace community in our ongoing efforts as the hub of human spaceflight. Presentations will focus on the ways in which these challenges, and the associated opportunities, can be leveraged by Houston’s innovation community. We will continue to identify potential space/terrestrial technologies of interest to Human Spaceflight.  Past NASA Tech Talks have included topics such as: From Space to Startup: Leveraging NASA Technology and Innovation to Propel Your Growing Enterprise Disruptive Filter Technology for Spacecraft Water Treatment:  The New Promise of Graphene Lunar dust capture using novel multiplexed inertial filter Lunar Passive Fuel Cell Technologies: Microbes in Space

item.title: Author Talk with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon From Chicago
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Albert and Ethel Herzstein Theater on the Mady and Ken Kades Stage

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a night with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon from Chicago: The Untold Story of an American Reporter in Nazi Germany.      “Today we face an alarming upsurge in the spread of misinformation and attempts by powerful figures to discredit facts so they can seize control of our political and cultural narratives. These are threats American journalist Sigrid Schultz knew all too well. The Chicago Tribune’s Berlin bureau chief and primary foreign correspondent for Central Europe from 1925 to January 1941, Schultz witnessed Hitler’s rise to power and was one of the first reporters—male or female—to warn American readers of the growing dangers of Nazism.  She was one of the last to leave Berlin before it was too late.     In The Dragon From Chicago, historian Pamela Toler tells the story of Schultz’s years spent courageously reporting the news from Berlin, from the revolts of 1919 through the Nazi rise to power and Allied air raids over Berlin in 1941. At a time when women reporters rarely wrote front-page stories, Schultz regularly  reported the truth about Nazi Germany in the face of censorship and the threat of expulsion, internment, or death. The Nazis called Schultz “that dragon from Chicago.” One of her fellow correspondents called her “Adolph Hitler’s greatest enemy.” Schultz herself claimed to be “just a reporter.” Her story is a powerful account of one woman standing up for truth in an era marked by the spread of disinformation and propaganda spawned by hate.”     Books will be available for purchase by credit card.

item.title: Houston Museum of Natural Science
item.description:
Sunday, August 30, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: Levy Park (Event Pavilion), TX

The Houston Museum of Natural Science comes to Levy Park to offer an opportunity to learn firsthand from Museum experts. Encounter real specimens and artifacts from the museum collection in an intimate, educational atmosphere. May 31: Rocks and Minerals Explore the fascinating characteristics of the most important building blocks of Earth’s crust. July 26: Energy Exciting demonstrations explore the remarkable forms of energy we encounter every day. August 30: Dinosaur Discovery Peek into the thrilling daily life of the dinosaur: investigate what dinosaurs ate, how they hunted, and the adaptations they developed to survive in a harsh prehistoric world. September 27: Birds Encounter an amazing variety of birds and discover their fascinating ancestral roots, while learning about their adaptations for success. October 25: Ancient Egypt From mummies to the pyramids, experience amazing architectural and cultural aspects of Ancient Egypt. November 29: Little Bodies, Big Jobs! Brings a selection of live arthropods from the Cockrell Butterfly Center to your classroom. Audiences of all ages will have a unique opportunity to meet some of the hardest workers in the invertebrate world up close and personal. December 13:  Astronomy  Investigate our place in space and ways we study this exciting place full of planets, moons, stars, and galaxies.

item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Friday, September 11, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

item.description:

Architecture Walks begin at 6 p.m. in June, July, August and September.The William A. Wilson Realty Co. began developing Woodland Heights in 1907 on 136 acres of land that was once part of John Austin's Mexican land grant. The neighborhood was one of Houston's first "streetcar suburbs" — a streetcar line ran from downtown along Houston Avenue to just outside the Woodland Heights gates, enabling working-class Houstonians to live in a lovely wooded setting and easily commute to their jobs.

item.title: National Voter Registration Day
item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: Houston Food Bank East Branch, 535 Portwall Street, Houston, TX, 77029, United States

Did you know that on Tuesday, September 15th, it’s National Voter Registration Day! At Houston Food Bank, we care about having your voice heard, and we are proud to provide the opportunity for you to register to vote on National Voter Registration Day! We are partnering with Harris County Tax Office and the National Voter Registration Day organization to serve as a site for Voter Registration at our Portwall location. You are eligible to register to vote if: You are a United States citizen; You are a resident of the county where you submit the application; You are at least 17 years and 10 months old on the date your voter registration application is submitted, and you are 18 years of age on Election Day. You are not a convicted felon (you may be eligible to vote if you have completed your sentence, probation, and parole); and You have not been declared by a court exercising probate jurisdiction to be either totally mentally incapacitated or partially mentally incapacitated without the right to vote. item.title: Unified Topgolf Pro-Am (Houston-Katy)
item.description:
Friday, September 18, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Topgolf-Katy, 1030 Memorial Brook Blvd, Houston, TX 77084, Houston, 77084

The Unified Topgolf Pro-Am is one of the most exciting and meaningful community partnership events hosted by Special Olympics Texas, bringing together athletes, families, coaches, volunteers, corporate partners, and local business leaders for an unforgettable day of golf, laughter, connection, and community impact. Each bay includes a Special Olympics Texas athlete paired alongside five golfers, creating a truly unique experience where relationships, memories, and meaningful moments are built throughout the day. From friendly competition and team spirit to incredible conversations and shared experiences, the event is designed to bring people together in a fun and welcoming environment while directly supporting local athletes and programs. Proceeds from the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am help provide year-round sports training, competitions, health initiatives, leadership development, and educational opportunities for children, teenagers, and adults with intellectual disabilities throughout the greater Houston area. As the event continues growing each year, the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am has quickly become a tremendous opportunity for organizations and community members to make a real impact while being part of something incredibly energetic, uplifting, and memorable. For more information regarding sponsorship opportunities, team entries, volunteer involvement, or sponsorship opportunities, please reach out to Jared Kossover, Strategic Partnerships Manager with Special Olympics Texas Jared Kossover E: jkossover@sotx.org C: 737-867-9659

item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

item.title: Unexpected Routes: Refugee Writers in Mexico
item.description:
Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Albert and Ethel Herzstein Theater

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for an evening lecture featuring Dr. Tabea Linhard, author of Unexpected Routes: Refugee Writers in Mexico. Unexpected Routes chronicles the refugee journeys of six writers whose lives were upended by fascism in the aftermath of the Spanish Civil War and during World War II. During her lecture, Dr. Linhard will explore the stories of German author Ruth Rewald, who was murdered during the Holocaust, and Czech writer and journalist Egon Erwin Kisch, who wrote about the Holocaust while in Mexico. While the writers she discusses in the book came from different backgrounds and wrote in different languages, they all made sense of their forced displacement in works that reveal their conflicted relationships with the people and places they encountered in transit as well as in Mexico. The literary output of these brilliant, prolific, but also flawed individuals reflects the most salient contradictions of what it meant to escape from fascistoccupied Europe. This event is free and open to the public but advanced registration is required.

As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. item.title: Houston TCG Con XII
item.description:
Friday, October 2, 2026 at 3 PM

Houston TCG Con XII – Find It. Trade It. Collect It. If you’ve been sitting on trade bait, chasing a grail, or just need to restock staples before the next format shift, this is your weekend. Houston TCG Con XII is three days of curated buying, selling, and trading across every major game – the vendors across the table are collectors just like you, and they’re buying out of your binder while you shop theirs.   📅 Friday, October 2 to Sunday, October 4, 2026 ⏰ Friday 3PM – 10PM | Saturday 10AM – 5PM | Sunday 10AM – 5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 🃏 Dozens of Vendor Tables – One Curated Floor Forget the rows of random tables. Houston TCG Con XII brings together vendors with serious depth across Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, MTG, One Piece, Lorcana, Riftbound, Flesh and Blood, Dragon Ball Super, Digimon, and more. Different games, different collections, one very busy floor.   🤝 Buy • Sell • Trade — All Weekend This is a buy-sell-trade floor, not a one-way shopping trip. The vendors here are collectors first.   🔍 On-Site Grading Submissions & Card Restorations — Cappy’s Cards! Have a card you’ve been thinking about grading? Or one that needs a little restoration? Cappy’s Cards will be on-site helping collectors with grading submissions, restoration services, and expert insight all weekend.   💼 Interested in Vending? If you’ve got singles, sealed product, graded slabs, TCG accessories, or anything else the Houston community is hunting this Labor Day weekend, apply here → https://tinyurl.com/HoustonTCGCon   🏨 Staying the Weekend? Three days is worth the trip. Book your stay: Here   Your binder has three days of work ahead of it. Lots of Pokémon, MTG, One Piece, Yu-Gi-Oh!, and more give you plenty to dig through, trade around, and bring home at Houston TCG Con XII.

item.title: Speakeasy Casino Night
item.description:
Friday, October 2, 2026 at 6 PM

Houston Heights Association · Est. 1973 SpeakeasyCasino Nightin the Heights One night, back in the Prohibition era. Casino tables, cocktails, live entertainment, a silent auction and raffle — and the whole neighborhood in one room. Every dollar stays in the Heights. DateFriday, October 2, 2026 Time7:00 – 10:30 pm WhereThe Historic Houston Heights Fire Station107 W 12th Street, Houston, TX 77008 Admission$100 per guestIncludes gaming chips, food & drink Get tickets — $100 Become an underwriter Admission One night only Speakeasy Ticket $100per guest Entry for one, 7:00 to 10:30 pm Starting stack of gaming chips for the tables Heavy hors d’oeuvres and cocktails Live entertainment and dancing Access to the silent auction and raffle How many are coming? − + 1 ticket $100.00 Add to cart → The evening What the night looks like Doors at seven, password at the door. Come dressed for 1926 if you like — flapper, pinstripe, or just your good jacket. Casino tables Blackjack, roulette, poker and craps, run by dealers all evening. Chips come with your ticket. Cocktails & bites Period cocktails at the bar and heavy hors d’oeuvres circulating all night. Silent auction & raffle Neighborhood-donated packages, experiences and prizes — bid from your table. Live entertainment Music, dancing, and a stage program — plus a few surprises we’re not printing here. Why it matters A $40,000 night for the neighborhood Casino Night is a fundraiser first. What we raise on October 2 goes directly into the programs neighbors actually see — the boulevard, the parks, the constable patrol, the home tour, and the small grants we make each spring. More than 150 residents and guests are expected. The Houston Heights Association is a volunteer-led nonprofit, and this is one of the few nights a year the whole neighborhood is in one room. $40,000Fundraising goal 150+Neighbors expected 100%Stays in the Heights Sponsorship Put your name on the night Three underwriting levels, each with tickets included and your name or logo on event materials, signage and communications. item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

item.title: Park to Port Bike Ride
item.description:
Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Bayou Parkland, 6532 Almeda Rd, Houston, TX, 77021, United States

Hermann Park Conservancy’s 12th annual Park to Port Bike Ride, presented by Port Houston, is set for Saturday, October 24. The 20-mile round-trip bike ride takes cyclists from Hermann Park’s Bayou Parkland along the Bayou Greenway trail all the way to Mason Park, near the Port of Houston. Enjoy the turn-around party, but be sure to save some energy for a well-deserved post-ride party under the Bill Coats Bridge! Park to Port is open to riders of all skill levels and is not a race. Whether you are an experienced cyclist or are riding just for fun, you can go at your own pace on this scenic city journey. Your participation in Park to Port supports Hermann Park Conservancy and its stewardship efforts for one of Houston’s most beloved parks while promoting the ever-growing Bayou Greenway trail system. Register and learn more at the following link: 12th Annual Park to Port Bike Ride. Early bird pricing is available until August 17. SPECIAL OFFER: Save $10 on registration when you sign up for BOTH the Park to Port Bike Ride and Run in the Park! Bundle deal is available via the link above. 🚗🏁 Houston World of Hot Wheels V | From Redlines to Racecars 🏁🚗 The weather is cooling down, but the diecast hunt is heating up. Thirty thousand cars can make a very long shopping list! Houston World of Hot Wheels V brings the diecast community together this October for a massive weekend of Hot Wheels, Matchbox, vintage pieces, customs, racing, trading, and collector discoveries.   📅 October 24-25 | 10AM–5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 EVENT HIGHLIGHTS 🔥 🛒 Hot Wheels Swap & Shop | Both Days 50+ vendors. 30,000+ diecast cars. One serious collector hunt. Dig through Hot Wheels, Matchbox, M2, Greenlight, Johnny Lightning, premium Car Culture, vintage pieces, redlines, MOC collectibles, loose mainlines, Super Treasure Hunts, Treasure Hunts, and more.   👶 Mini Zones & Family Fun Younger collectors and first-time racers have plenty to explore, with family-friendly spaces designed to make the weekend fun for every generation of diecast fan.   🚨 Vendors Wanted Have STHs, vintage redlines, customs, premium diecast, or boxes of mainlines ready to move? Houston World of Hot Wheels V is looking for vendors bringing cars collectors actually want to dig through. 📥 Apply: https://tinyurl.com/CCSGuestVendorFromHouston   👥 We’re Looking for Collaborators 🕹️ Activity Hosts → https://forms.gle/74Qvuv9PFzeDVF1V8 🙌 Volunteer Sign-Up → https://forms.gle/15zMGTqZPSGKjGdy6   🏨 Traveling to Houston? Special hotel rates are available for attendees traveling in for the weekend. Book here 👉🏻 https://www.marriott.com/event-reservations/reservation-link.mi?id=1767823967549&key=CORP&app=resvlink   Hunt the cars. Race the cars. Trade the cars. Build a collection nobody else has. October is rolling in hot.

item.title: CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational
item.description:
Friday, November 13, 2026 at 10 AM

🏆 CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational – 2026 Series Overview The CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational is a year-long competitive circuit for Riftbound players. The season concludes on November 13–15, 2026 in Houston, Texas with a $50,000 Invite-Only Championship featuring 128 of the best players in the game.   LEADERBOARD ↓   🗓️ Date: November 13-15, 2026 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St, #1500, Houston, TX 77036   🏁 How to Qualify for the $50,000 Invitational ✅ 3 Ways to Qualify for the 128-Player Invitational: Qualification Path Spots 🏆 Auto-Qualify – Top 8 from each $25K Main Event (6 total events) 48 📈 Points Leaderboard – Top performers across all events 64 🔥 LCQ Winners – Winner of each Last Chance Qualifier (16 total) 16 Total 128 If a player qualifies through multiple methods, leaderboard spots roll down to the next eligible player.   🎖️ Bonus for the Most Consistent Players At the end of the season, the Top 8 players on the Points Leaderboard will receive a Round 1 Bye in the Invitational. This rewards dedication, consistency, and season-long performance.   📅 Main Qualifier Weekends – Structure & Prize Pools Each of the 6 qualifier weekends includes two events:   🔹 Saturday – $25,000 Guaranteed Main Event Format: Standard Swiss + Top Cut Top 8 auto-qualify for the CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational Top 128 placements earn leaderboard points   🔸 Sunday – $5,000 Guaranteed Side Event One-day competitive event Top 8 earn 30 points each No auto-invite from this event   📈 Leaderboard Point System 🏆 Saturday $25K Main Events – Top 128 Earn Points Placement Points 1st – 100 2nd – 80 3rd–4th – 65 5th–8th – 50 9th–16th – 35 17th–32nd – 20 33rd–64th – 10 65th–128th – 5 ➡️ Total points per Main Event: 1,750 ➡️ Total points across 6 events: 10,500 🔸 Sunday $5K Events – Top 8 Earn 30 Points Each   🔥 Last Chance Qualifiers (LCQs) 16 LCQ events held leading up to the Invitational Winner of each LCQ earns an automatic invite Open entry — no prior points or placement required   📍 Main Qualifier Tournament Weekends (6 Total) All dates and locations as scheduled for the 2026 CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational season.   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #1 January 31 – February 1, 2026 📍 Houston, Texas Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗 https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-houston-invitational-qualifier-1   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #2 March 13–15, 2026 📍 Houston, Texas Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗  https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-houston-invitational-qualifier-2   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #3 May 23–24, 2026 📍 Atlanta, Georgia Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗 https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-houston-invitational-qualifier-3   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #4 July 18–19, 2026 📍 Atlanta, Georgia Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗 https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-atlanta-invitational-qualifier-4   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #5 September 19–20, 2026 📍 Houston, Texas Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗 https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-houston-invitational-qualifier-5   🗓️ Qualifier Weekend #6 October 10-11, 2026 📍 Atlanta, Georgia Saturday – $25,000 Main Event Sunday – $5,000 Side Event (Top 8 earn 30 pts each) 🔗 https://topdeck.gg/event/25000-atlanta-invitational-qualifier-6   🏆 CCS $50,000 Riftbound Invitational Championship Weekend 🗓️ November 13–15, 2026 📍 Houston, Texas Saturday & Sunday – $50,000 Main Event Sunday – Scaling $5,000 Side Event Last Chance Qualifiers – All Day Friday   128 players compete for $50,000 and the title of CCS Riftbound Champion.

item.title: Run in the Park
item.description:
Saturday, November 14, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Molly Ann Smith Plaza, Hermann Park, Houston, TX, 77004, United States

Hermann Park Conservancy’s Run in the Park will return on Saturday, November 14. Participants will be able to run, or walk, to support the conservation efforts of the Conservancy. All proceeds from Run in the Park go towards the crucial work needed to maintain Hermann Park and its trail system. With 5K and 10K routes, as well as a 1K kids’ route for the in-person event, exercise enthusiasts of all ages and abilities can come to explore the Park and enjoy the shaded trails enjoyed by millions of visitors per year. The event starts and ends at the Molly Ann Smith Plaza, near the Jones Reflection Pool, and includes a post-run party with food, drinks, music, and more! The Conservancy also offers an at-home, virtual option. You can support Hermann Park at your own pace, from the comfort of your own neighborhood! Virtual registrants will still get the exclusive Run in the Park t-shirt and access to an online leaderboard. Register and learn more at the following link: 23rd Annual Run in the Park. Early bird pricing is available until August 14. SPECIAL OFFER: Save $10 on registration when you sign up for BOTH the Park to Port Bike Ride and Run in the Park! Bundle deal is available via the link above. Information on Run in the Park can be found here.

From Hermann Park Conservancy

item.title: Houston TCG Con XIII
item.description:
Friday, November 20, 2026 at 3 PM

Houston TCG Con XIII – Another Weekend, Another Hunt The hobby doesn’t slow down for the holidays; it just gets more interesting. Houston TCG Con XIII brings the community together for another big weekend of cards, collecting, and trading. Bring your binder, bring your trades, and bring that card you’ve been sitting on since summer. You never know who’s been looking for exactly what you’ve got.   📅 November 20 – 22, 2026 ⏰ Friday 3PM – 10PM | Saturday & Sunday 10AM – 5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 Every Major TCG on One Houston Floor Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, MTG, One Piece, Lorcana, Riftbound, Dragon Ball Super, Digimon, Flesh and Blood – the full lineup, curated vendor by vendor. Singles, sealed ETBs, booster boxes, and collection boxes. Graded slabs from PSA, SGC, CGC, and BGS. Japanese imports and OCG product. Vintage and WOTC-era Pokémon. Competitive staples for current formats. Starter-friendly product for collectors just getting into their first game. Whatever you’re hunting, it’s on a table this weekend.   📁 Bring the Binder – the Vendors Are Buying Too This is a buy-sell-trade floor, not a one-way shopping trip. The vendors here are collectors first. They’re working buylists, moving bulk, and trading out of attendee binders right alongside everyone else. Show up with the specs you’ve been sitting on. Come ready to deal.   🔍 On-Site Grading Submissions & Card Restorations — Cappy’s Cards! Have a card you’ve been thinking about grading? Or one that needs a little restoration? Cappy’s Cards will be on-site helping collectors with grading submissions, restoration services, and expert insight all weekend.   🎴 New to the Hobby? Start Here. Every game represented, vendors who genuinely enjoy explaining the hobby, and zero pressure. Houston TCG Con has always been the room where serious collectors and first-timers coexist without either feeling out of place. Bring the friend who’s been curious. Bring the kid who just cracked their first pack.   🛒 Interested in Vending? Guest vendor tables are open. If you’ve got singles, sealed product, graded slabs, TCG accessories, or anything else the community is hunting this season, apply here → https://tinyurl.com/HoustonTCGCon   Staying the Weekend? Three days is worth the trip. Book your stay: Here   The year may be winding down, but the hobby isn’t. Houston TCG Con XIII is bringing the community together for another big weekend of cards, collecting, and trading, with one floor and every major TCG!

From CCS Houston
